title: Large personal Oric, TI99, 6502 and 6809 tooling discovery
summary: Personally screen 111 candidate URLs and add 26 projects, with nine explicit non-promotion decisions.
notes: Root assistant personally screened 36 search routes yielding 111 unique candidate URLs, reviewed 35 candidates and prepared 26 additions plus 9 non-promotions for direct-main publication without a worker, PR or branch. Scope includes Oric tape formats, TI99 GPL/disk tools, Atari ST media, MSX graphics, 6502 analyzers, 6809 assemblers and multi-platform reconstruction. Partial portfolio code, linear-sweep limitations, experimental profiles and legacy build dependencies are explicitly qualified. No upstream builds, games or physical disk operations were executed. Large or encoding-mismatched files retain immutable source links rather than altered proof excerpts.

sources.reason: Bidirectional data/WAV tools encode and recover Oric slow-mode tape framing and synchronization.
CLI changes BASIC/assembly type and autorun flags, and displays name/load-address information from Oric TAP headers.
Decodes GPL and FMT bytecodes, with optional per-subroutine FETC payload lengths to keep inline data out of instruction listings.
Browser converter maps PNG pixels into Spectrum screen/TAP data, offers ink/paper assignment strategies and highlights attribute-clash errors.
Image conversion library and CLI/GTK frontend perform color-space reduction, attribute selection and SCR/BMP/ZXP output, including ULAplus and Timex modes.
Converts SCR bitmap data into an 8192-byte TRS-80 semigraphics character map using packed pixel groups.
Published engineering excerpt implements two-pass assembly, addressing-mode encoding and C integration for stepping a Musashi 68000 core with TRAP 15 console services.
Python APIs assemble code, share object maps/symbols with disassembly and simulation, and enable host-programmed instrumentation instead of an assembler macro language.
Traces supplied code entry points and references, annotates code/data reads and writes, emits call graphs and xa-style assembly.
Models registers and memory, dispatches instruction classes and prints single-step disassembly/register traces.
Standalone Python script emits addressed hex/mnemonic listings for documented MOS 6502 instructions and common operand forms.
Ports classic dis6502 ideas to Python with traced code, named arrays/pointers, structured symbol files and Lunar Lander/vector-display annotation material.
Table-driven script translates raw bytes to 6502 mnemonics, handles branch offsets and emits BYTE directives for unknown values.
Headless Ghidra pipelines recover bank-qualified instructions, pointer/dispatch structures and secondary CPU payloads, then emit modular assembler projects with rebuild manifests.
GFA BASIC program reads ST/MSA images, handles compressed tracks and writes/formats physical floppy tracks through Atari system calls.
Builds FAT disk contents from a host directory or ZIP and writes raw/RLE-compressed MSA tracks with size-dependent geometry choices.
Executes supported PSID/RSID player code in a compact 6510/C64 runtime, captures frame-level SID state and converts inferred musical events to MIDI.
Converts common image files to SCREEN 2/5/6/7/8/12 binary layouts with palette selection, dithering, tile and selected-region export.
SDL converter optimizes two-color pixel-row fragments, builds tile patterns/color bytes and exports SCREEN 2 data with adjustable color/error handling.
Manages TI floppy/hard-disk image layouts, allocation and files, with BASIC and GPL/native-code analysis components.
TI client reads disk sectors and sends checksummed 256-byte blocks to a Windows receiver, with allocated-sector or full-disk modes.
Machine profiles orchestrate Greaseweazle backup/restore/verify workflows and include ATR header wrapping/stripping and custom TI format definitions.
Emulates CPC 464/664/6128 CPU and devices with disk/tape reading, snapshots, host-text injection, integrated debugger and sound analysis.
QuickLook generator parses .P program state into authentic-style BASIC listings, saved screens and generated cassette audio.
Preserves a one-pass interactive 6809 assembler for N88-BASIC86, derived from FM-new7 work, alongside a modern structural Python rewrite.
Python assembly DSL represents instructions, labels, addressing and data directives, then resolves multipass output into address-keyed code fragments.
README describes planned architecture and canvas implementation is a placeholder; no implemented sprite editor established.
Repository contains README and license without the described disk tooling implementation.
CMake skeleton and main returning zero do not implement the advertised DOS game data diagnosis.
README-only project; no save parsing or editor implementation established.
Supporting ROM research is in an Excel workbook not directly inspected in this pass. Defer content review rather than infer a complete annotated disassembly from the repository name.
GitHub metadata identifies fork of tracked drmortalwombat/oscar64. README retains upstream identity and reviewed tree/compiler source do not establish a distinct Oric implementation.
README and license only; no snapshot analyzer implementation found.
